evidence_proposition: MIL-STD-1220B identifies MIL-M-23573 as the military specification for chelated monoethanolamine intended for CO2-scrubbing equipment; MIL-P-24082C independently specifies aqueous chelated MEA as the absorbent in the submarine Mark IIIB CO2-removal plant.
limitations: The 1991 MIL-STD-1220B corroborates the material specification and military scrubbing purpose; MIL-P-24082C supplies the 1981 submarine-equipment link. Neither establishes installation on a particular boat, vapor concentration, individual exposure, route, dose, symptoms, or causation. The modern Sigma SDS is hazard information, not historical supply evidence.

submarine_evidence: National Academies Submarine Contaminants Volume 2 — benzene chapter
evidence_proposition: NRC reviews benzene as a submarine contaminant and reports limited air sampling: detected during one-time sampling on two submarines and not detected in a similar exercise on two others.
limitations: NRC explicitly cautions that these one-time measurements on four submarines may not represent the submarine fleet. They do not establish concentration or exposure for a particular boat or sailor. The Sigma SDS does not establish shipboard product use.

submarine_evidence: GAO HRD-80-2 Navy Efforts To Protect Workers From Asbestos Exposure
evidence_proposition: GAO documents Navy-ship asbestos insulation history; Navy information in the report states asbestos-free materials were approved for the last two SSN-637-class submarine propulsion plants in 1972, demonstrating the preceding asbestos-to-nonasbestos transition context.
limitations: Asbestos comprises multiple fibrous minerals and products; a chrysotile SDS is not a universal asbestos sheet. Class-level/history evidence does not prove asbestos type, location, condition, disturbance, or individual exposure on a particular submarine.

hazard_reference: Sigma/Supelco DBP identity/SDS lead; DBNP Sigma-hosted marketplace identity lead
submarine_evidence: National Academies Submarine Contaminants Volume 2 — DBNP chapter
evidence_proposition: NRC identifies DBP as an antioxidant formerly present in TEP 2190 and describes electrostatic-precipitator nitration as a pathway generating DBNP; NRC reports NAVSEA changed the 2190 TEP specification in 1993 to limit DBP to no more than 10 ppm. ASSIST independently identifies MIL-PRF-17331 as the governing 2190 TEP/O-250 specification family.
limitations: The 2190 TEP specification-family link and NRC pathway do not establish DBNP presence or concentration on a particular boat or individual exposure. NRC reports insufficient data to derive DBNP submarine guidance levels. Current specification language must not be projected backward except where NRC independently documents the historical change; modern Sigma/Supelco references do not establish historical supplier or product use.
